comment: I took him for Macro. He is nice and wants you to do well, but he's also bad at explaining things. His tests are fair and there is not much homework outside of class besides some problem sets and readings. Lectures feel very long. Lots of group work. You may have to rely on textbook readings and tutors in order to understand concepts.
He was very funny and got his points across well. If you are looking to take Econ I recommend him.

I took this class with no prior experience in MicroEcon, and I had to rely on youtube videos for most of my learning. The classes felt like hours long due to the lecture heavy atmosphere. The tests are that close to what we learn in class which was frustrating, but ended up doing ok.

Although he is a great guy and clearly tries his best, his lectures can be very boring and hard to sit through. Often goes on random tangents that are not necessary. His tests and assignments are never super hard, but the wording is often confusing.

Professor Heinicke is a good professor, knows a lot about economics and cares about his students. The class is very lecture heavy which are sometimes hard to follow with group work sometimes. The homework is kind of confusing and his grading is specific but the tests are pretty fair. Decent professor for Econ if you already have some understanding
Cant explain things but tries his best
He is pretty nice. Tough tests

He is a professor who clearly cares about and is interested in economics. He takes the time to explain concepts in detail and adds several, often unrelated anecdotes. This can lead to his lectures being pretty long and a little boring but he does explain things well and is clearly passionate about his craft.

He is such a lovable character, like walking on a cloud. Sometimes his lectures are a bit dull but they are very digestible and easy to understand. The textbook and videos are amazing, and if you follow those, you will do well in the class. Lots of group work doing application problems, but it's only during class time and are helpful for tests.

His tests are so easy if you study the material. His lectures are a bit boring, but he was so sweet and genuinely wanted to teach his students. There is some outside homework and easy group discussions in class. Definitely an attainable A. He is a good guy and is very accessible outside of class. Take him!

I've never taken econ and I don't regret taking Dr. H's class at all! He is a little slower with lectures and to be honest, you will learn more outside of the class in the textbook and videos than in his lectures but I always felt confident enough to raise my hand. His office hours are greta too. Open note quizzes, tests look like the practice.

I would not take this class if you want to pursue economics. He was very confusing and I felt like I learned less than I when I came into the class. Really nice guy, but take someone else if you can. The class is not too much work and is a fine option if you don't need to master the subject.
Very boring and mid teacher. Lectures are a snooze-fest but he randomly crashing out every week which is hilarious to watch

Where to begin... Nice guy but makes everything overly complex. The class format alternates lectures with daily group work, which balances quizzes, but tests count way too heavily. I was confused from day one; office hours didn't help. Lectures are incredibly boring (40-60min/day) – you'd learn more from a 5min YouTube video. Avoid if possible.
lectures can make material seem more confusing, but textbook and videos help a lot. class can be slow but we work in groups a lot. grading is fair, quizzes in class and three exams.

His quizzes for each new topic make can definitely help save a lot of your grade since they are multiple choices and open book. For his tests, it is all about figuring out how to answer his questions. I got B on both my tests, but still got an A in the course (I don't know my final exam score though).

When teach he often confuses himself/cannot explain basic concepts properly. I am someone who took AP Microeconomics in high school and did extremely well, but still find his class difficult. He doesn't give any busy work, and gives out review packets before the test which are very helpful, but he is a very tough grader.

Dr. Heinicke is very funny and sweet, but he is not a very good teacher. His assignments and tests are not clear in regards to instructions, and if you have no foundation in economics, you will struggle. There are only 2 tests, but they are not worth a lot of you grade. Does not keep gradebook updated and group work plays a large role in the grade.

Likable guy but a boring lecturer who is not good at explaining basic econ - if a student asked a straightforward question it seemed like everyone understood what was being asked but him and he would often leave the class more confused than we entered. tries his best to keep class fun, and can be funny in a dad joke way but is not a good professor.

If you aren't naturally good at econ, do not take this course. He is a really nice guy, but the tests were not straight forward. Additionally, lots of your final grad is based on group quizzes, so good if you have a good group, and bad if you don't.

In Heinicke's Econ 101, You don't learn economics you learn about Heinicke's brain. He is funny and cool, but you will leave class knowing LESS than before. You are probably better off missing every class and relying on old exams and quizzes. Heinicke is a likable guy, but don't plan on learning economics in this class.

Dr. Heinicke is very sweet and passionate about economics. However, he does make his tests harder than the problems you do in class. He will take off points for minor things and is looking for a very specific explanation for problems. Overall, he is a good professor, but you definitely have to share his love for economics to enjoy the class.

Heinicke is a nice guy, but he should not be a professor anymore. He does flipped classroom, which means you learn from reading a textbook and videos he posts. He tries to be funny in class by telling economics jokes, but it's a snooze. I'm not lying when I say a kid fell asleep on the first day of class. Do not take him.

Dr. Heinicke is a very nice person who is always enthusiastic about teaching and helping his students. However, prepares for a lot of readings and self-studying because his way of teaching is very confusing. He is also a tough grader so prepare to learn his key words as well.

Nice and tries to be funny but bro forgets what he's talking about and is impossible to follow. I will look back on this class and laugh because of how boring and dumb this class was, but being in class is like watching paint dry and watching a man ramble about economics, thinking we are following. This isn't just me either, the whole class talks

hes okay. He can be very boring and very slow making it so hard to follow along. he knows his stuff but since its mostly lecture with a bit of group work it can be hard to check if you understand the concepts. i wish we had more in class participation and if it was faster paced. very interesting guy. don't take him at 9 am

Currently sitting in his class and have to say he is by far the most boring professor I have taken in awhile. His lectures wander and though he is passionate about the subject, I often find it does not translate well to teaching students. His tests aren't hard, so thats a plus, but personally, I enjoy a more upbeat and engaging teacher.

Professor Heinicke is a great guy and very passionate about economics and you can tell he knows a lot. The majority of the homework involves textbook readings and that ends up being the material you use to study for tests. His lectures, although very well planned, are hard to follow and his teaching style can be confusing.

Professor Heinicke knows a ton about economics and has lots of experience teaching. Hes a very funny professor which is great but he tends to explain things in ways that either make it more difficult to understand or just with bad explanations in general. The workload isn't a ton and the class is easy if you study a moderate amount before exams.

He can be a little hard to follow because he goes off on tangent a lot but if you do the reading carefully before class, those little details can be helpful. He grades pretty hard so pay attention to the key words he usually uses. Really accessible and nice outside of class.
Super nice professor, but really tough to follow. Classes can be confusing because he goes off on tangents. He does make funny jokes and is always excited to teach his students.
Such a nice guy, but very confusing. Not the best lecturer and tends to over complicate questions students ask.
Great guy; really hard to follow. He tends to assume we already know basics of economics which wasn't the case for me. Can't emphasize enough how good of a person he is, though. Great jokes as well.
He gives lots of group quizzes and the tests are all open note which was very helpful. He cares about his students and makes good jokes.

The class was not always interesting, but lots of group work and the tests were extremely manageable. At least this year with covid all tests were open book. He definitely knows his stuff but it's very easy to zone out. I would say I did most of my learning from the textbook and he was there to supplement explanations. Easy A imo

Very boring. Lectures a lot. Textbook reading is most of the homework and he gives very few tests and graded assignments. Is very knowledgable and helpful in class. Is unclear what information is more important than others but very nice guy.

Dr. Heinicke is extremely knowledgeable regarding economics, but he is SO BORING and vague in his lectures. I would strongly not recommend him to annoying planning on continuing on in economics as I would not feel prepared for higher-leveled Econ courses. The way he sets up quizzes is good and you often get to work with an assigned team.

Probably the one professor I had last semester that handled the pandemic the best. He was incredible understanding, and even gave out extra credit points on the final exam. I have never been great at econ, but I still got an A in the class due to his conscious grading, even while things were online. He is the fairest prof I've had thus far.

Heinicke's a great teacher, but his class wasn't the best. He's a quirky guy and his lectures are boring but he really wants to see his students do well. HW isn't graded but you've gotta read and master concepts on your own to get by. His tests are a bit difficult too but if you work hard you'll do fine. Take Heinicke if you don't want lots of HW.

He is extremely confusing during his lectures and tests are worded unclearly. He grades tests harshly and is always looking for specific wording of answers, and makes it nearly impossible to get full credit on tests. He expects you to read the textbook and fully comprehend everything for class where he fails to explain the topics. Don't take him!
He is awful at explaining the topics, it's better to just not ask questions because you will be more confused than when you started.
This just ain't it chief. Left me more confused from when I started.

Professor Heinicke is incredible. My day is instantly made whenever I have the pleasure of encountering him. I cannot emphasize enough the quality and passion of his teaching. He displays immense expertise and art in explaining complex subjects such as elasticity, insurance, and marginal utility. I wish I could enroll in his class every semester.
Worst teacher I've ever had in my life had to teach myself I hope he gets fired
if you put in a tiny amount of work you'll be fine, and is super available outside of class- really makes an effort to get to know students and their personal interests
DO NOT TAKE HIM. Absolute worst teacher I have ever taken. Does not explain concepts clearly and is so so boring.

He doesn't do a good job of explaining concepts, so if you are good at teaching yourself from the textbook then you will be fine. Tests are significantly harder than any practice problems or examples done in class.

A really funny guy that pops out the most spontaneous comments and material from time to time. The class is pretty straight forward, you got group quizzes and problem sets that are nearly 25% of your final grade and the final is basically like a 3rd test. Nevertheless, the classes are mostly snoozers due to the monotony his teaching style.

Great guy, quirky but funny. three tests all year all pretty straight forward and easy. quizzes pretty often, but only 10 questions or so, open note. Then you take the quiz again in a group and both grades go in the grade book. Take this professor

Dr. Heinicke does not give clear explanation to the easiest concept. His lectures are boring and not intellectual at all. I always fall asleep. His test questions are weird and if you do not answer it the way he wanted, you fail. No way I am taking his course again!!

I generally really enjoy Economics, he made me hate the whole idea about it. I think of myself as a pretty determined student, but this class was insanely boring and unengaging. I learn best  in an environment where the teacher is good at actually teaching. He can not teach. I had to teach myself everything from the textbook.

Taking him at 9 was a mistake. The majority of the  class is asleep however, he knows what he's teaching. He's very knowledgable and the tests are certainly easy as long as you keep up with the homework and actually do all that is requested of you. He is a genuinely nice guy and I would take him again as a professor. Non-cumulative final :)

I dread this class. Not because econ is difficult, but because the class is SO boring. Especially at 9 AM. I'd go for another professor if you're looking to get econ 101 out of the way. THere are three tests and he grades them pretty hard, he's weirdly specific about your answers. Say exactly what he would say or don't expect to get full points.

Extremely boring, but his tests are not that challenging. He barely assigns homework, and tries to make very bad jokes. He is so boring i dread his class. One problem set per semester is graded, which is right before the exam. Overall, not a tough teacher but very boring. Attendance is mandatory.
If you have taken a Marco or basic econ course before and enjoyeddid well in it than you are fine. Material is very basic, not hard at all. An easy A if you understand basic economics.
Class is like watching paint dry at times. However, theres very little work and he does cover all of the material. Tests can be tough

Heinicke isn't that great of a teacher. He obviously knows a lot about economics but he doesn't know how to explain complicated concepts to kids that have never learned econ before. Besides that, his class is easy. Only hmwk is reading like 5 pages per class, not too hard of a grader. If you make an effort to learn the concepts, you'll get an A
Probably the worst teacher I've ever had. He does not know how to explain anything. Would never take a class with him again.

Definitely a caring and attentive professor. If you seek outside help he will definitely recognize that and reward you for the effort that you put in. There are 3 exams, after the first you will realize that more is better when explaining your responses. Even though class is boring, he tries to make jokes and  I DEFINITELY RECOMMEND HIM.
Really boring class. The professor is unclear explaining concepts, and often tries to make some pathetic jokes to wake up his students.

This is a fairly easy class. There isn't much work, just some reading.  Class is usually interesting and he makes use of multiple class activities.  Tests and quizzes are fairly easy.  However, on written questions on the tests he rarely gives full credit.

Gets off track a lot but is good at explaining things in a context that makes it easy to remember and understand. Great classroom discussions and fun activities to demonstrate concepts. Disorganized but very funny

Dr. H is one of my favorite professors. Anyone who claims that he doesn't know the material is ridiculous, the man has a Ph.D in economic history from UofToronto. His class is a breeze if you read and pay attention, albeit getting full credit on test questions is a challenge. Definitely the guy you want for principles classes.
Very disorganized professor. Tends to get off topic in the middle of a lecture which makes him hard to follow at times. I've had to pretty much learn on my own. Not optimal.

Heinicke does his best to instill some interest into relatively dry material. He is easily the goofiest teacher I've ever had. Unfortunately, because of his quirky style, he can be very hard to follow at times. Hard to get full credit on test questions, but he does give alot of credit. Basically an easy "B" if you pay attention.
DO NOT TAKE FOR MACRO...AWFUL!

He is a very nice guy, but he is not a good teacher who barely understands what he is teaching. He is often confused by rudimentary questions and his shallow understanding of the material is revealed by his logically unsound answers. If you want to do well and get a basic understanding of the micro economy then take his class.
awesome teacher, knows what he's doing. homework and tests not too bad. gives good explanation. i recommend taking him for econ!

He's a great professor.  Really explains well, not easy for everything, but helps you understand. easy in the sense that people can understand everything so everyone does well!  GOOD professor to take!!
Really nice guy. Explains concepts well. And he gives good grades
easy to get a good grade, but kind of an awkward guy.  tries to be funny, but fails miserably.
